translations.text: The Evangelist Luke concluded this day's gospel in few words, but it is filled with the manifold power of the heavenly mystery.
That is, in our language: "After eight days had been fulfilled from the Lord's birth, so that he should be circumcised,
And I will set my covenant between me and you; and I will greatly multiply you, and you shall be the father of many nations.
Abraham stretched himself out with all his limbs on the ground, and God said to him, "Keep my covenant, you and your offspring after you, in their generations.
Every male child, when it is eight nights old, shall be circumcised, both the nobly born and the slave-born; and whoever neglects this, his soul shall perish, because he has made my covenant void.

so that there should be a sign on their bodies as a manifestation that they believed in God; and he commanded that he should take a sharp-edged flint and cut off a part of the skin at the front of his member.
And that sign was then as great among believing people as holy baptism is now, except only that no one could attain the kingdom of God,
the same one called out long ago through the old law: "Whatever male child is not circumcised in the foreskin of his flesh, his soul shall perish, because he has made my covenant void."
He said that he had not come in order to overthrow the old law, but to fulfil it.
and by that he showed that the old law was holy and good in its time for those who were obedient to it.
It is not now permitted to Christian people to keep this circumcision bodily; but nevertheless no one is truly Christian unless he keeps that circumcision in spiritual practices.
But let everyone know for certain that, unless he diminishes his fleshly desires and lust, he does not keep his Christianity with right observance.
But we who are created in God's likeness, and have an undying soul, shall rise from death and render to God an account of all our thoughts and words and deeds.
Therefore we must not be circumcised in one member only, but we must always diminish foul lust, and turn our eyes away from evil sights, and our ears from evil listening;
We have often heard that people call this day New Year's Day, as though this day were the first in the course of the year;

Some of our service-books begin at the Advent of the Lord; yet that is not therefore the beginning of the year, nor is it on this day by any reasoning, although our calendars begin again at this point.
that is, on the day on which the Hebrew people begin their count of the year, just as the leader Moses wrote in the books of the law.
Now the Hebrew people kept the first day of the year at the spring equinox, because on that day the yearly seasons were established.
The eighteenth day of the month that we call March, which you call Hlyda, was the first day of this world.
Now foolish people practise many kinds of divination on this day, in great error, after heathen custom, contrary to their Christianity,
but Monday is not the first of the days of the week; it is the second. Sunday is first in creation, in order, and in honour.
The Christianity of the man who spends his life in devilish divinations is worth nothing; he is disguised as a Christian man, and is a wretched heathen idolater;
